REPORT AT A GLANCE 
 
Offaly company Dotser wins Regional 
Enterprise Award 
Tullamore based Dotser has won the 
award for the Mid-East Region at this 
year’s 
National 
Enterprise 
Awards, 
organised by the Local Enterprise Offices 
to 
celebrate 
Ireland’s 
best 
small 
businesses. 
 
National Community Weekend 
On the 5th of May Offaly County Council 
held ‘The Big Hello’ a National Community 
Event that attracted over 3000 people to 
Lough Boora Discovery Park. Plenty of 
fun was had by all with a wide range of 
activities including welly throwing, Tug of 
War and Junk Drumming. The food was 
provided by local food suppliers and 
producers.  Children’s entertainment 
included face painting, arts and crafts, 
water zorbing, and all enjoyed the fine 
display of basket weaving. Many local 
groups assisted with operations at that 
event to ensure things ran smoothly. 
 
Traffic Count 
A Countywide Traffic Count on all 
Regional and strategic Local Roads was 
carried out in May. The information will 
inform Roads on traffic volumes for future 
schemes. 
 
Water Projects 
Contractors have been appointed to carry 
out upgrades and are on site in Clonaslee.  
A trial well is ongoing in Arden and the 
supplementary 
reservoir 
is 
under 
construction at Arden.  Once completed 
this project will provide safe and secure 
water supply for 18,000 local residents.

ENVIRONMENT AND WATER 
 
Water Services 
Offaly County Council deliver water 
services in accordance with the Service 
Level Agreement (SLA) with Irish Water 
(IW).  Water services are 100% funded by 
Irish Water who are now the statutory 
authority for water services and all major 
decisions around funding of services will be 
approved by IW.    The EPA Drinking Water 
Quality Report 2017 showed that Offaly had 
21 public supplies, Offaly had 98.6% 
microbiological compliance rate and a 99% 
chemical parameter compliance rate. 
 
Water Projects 
Water main rehabiliatation projects in 2018 
included Screggan, Mucklagh, Crinkle, 
Brosna South and Mountbolus.  The average 
unaccounted for water (UFW) in Offaly in 
2018 was 10,573m³/d. 
 
Tullamore and Birr Water Supply Scheme:  
Contractors have been appointed to carry out 
the upgrades and are on site in Clonaslee.  A 
trial well is ongoing in Arden and the 
supplementary 
reservoir 
is 
under 
construction at Arden.  Once completed this 
project will provide safe and secure water 
supply for 18,000 local residents.  The works 
will involve €21.5m investment in water 
infrastructure and will be carried out by Irish 
Water in partnership with OCC. 
 
Wastewater Projects 
Tullamore Sewerage Network – Drainage 
Area Plan & Sewer Rehabilitation Project. 
Cloghan, Banagher &Shinrone Wastewater 
Treatment Plants- Proposals to upgrade 
plants. 
 
Group Water Schemes 
Offaly County Council remains the Water 
Services Authority for GWS, Small Private 
Supplies and domestic wastewater treatment 
systems (septic tanks).   The Council 
continues to support the GWS sector in 
conjunction with the National Federation of 
GWS 
financially, 
administratively 
and 
technically.   Allocations for Rural Water 
Programme 2019-2021 will be announced 
mid to late June 2019.  Subsidy levels 
increased from Jan 2018 – max subsidy €231 
private schemes and €115 for public schemes 
(IW sources). 
 
Well Grants 
Under this scheme a residential property if 
more than 7 years old and not connected to 
either public or group scheme may be

Grant is subject to 75% of work, max grant 
€2,031.58.

Waterframework Directive (WFD) 
The River Basin Management Plan for 
Ireland 2018-2021 sets out current status of 
our waters and Ireland’s Implementation 
Strategy to comply with the requirements of 
this Directive, in conjunction with LAWPro 
Catchment Assessment Team and will focus 
on Priority Areas for Action (PAA).  The 
Water Quality Team in OCC are charged 
with undertaking assessments in the county 
where water quality is at risk of not achieving 
Good Status under the WFD.   Priority Areas 
for 
Action 
in 
Offaly 
include 
the 
Gaegeborough, Boora, Silver, Barrow, Little 
Brosna, Clareen and Ballyfinboy Upper.

(WWTS)

Climate Change & Energy Awareness 
This is a key area where OCC is required to 
show leadership in both promoting public 
awareness and in changing the mind-sets 
towards 
climate 
change 
and 
energy 
management.  The Climate Action and Low 
Carbon Development Act 2015 provides for 
approval of plans, a National Mitigation Plan 
and National Adaptation Framework by 
government in relation to climate change for 
the purpose of pursuing the transition to a 
low 
carbon, 
climate 
resilient 
and 
environmentally sustainable economy by 
2050. The strategy is currently being 
reviewed by Environmental Consultants for 
SEA and AA screening. The draft Strategy 
will go on public consultation in June 2019 
and a copy will be sent to Elected Members. 
The Offaly Climate Change Adaptation 
Strategy will be presented to the Elected 
Members of Offaly County Council for 
adoption in September 2019.

National Waste Collection Permit Office 
This office processes waste collection 
permits and currently holds a register of 2012 
waste collectors.  The NWCPO manages an 
on-line portal for gathering waste collection 
permit and waste facility annual return data 
which is used for local, regional and national 
waste reporting requirements.   The 
operation of the NWCPO is operated through 
ISO9001 standards and enhanced IT systems 
which ensures a high quality and robust 
service for stakeholders.   
 
ROADS 
 
The Roads Programme 2019  
The Roads Programme 2019 is ongoing 
throughout the County with significant 
progress in our Road Improvement schemes. 
The Surface Dressing commenced on 27th 
May and is currently in the Birr area moving 
to the Edenderry area in June.  
 
Traffic Count 
A Countywide Traffic Count on all Regional 
and strategic Local Roads was carried out in 
May. The information will inform Roads on 
traffic volumes for future schemes. 
 
TII Pavement scheme 
The TII Pavement scheme on the N52, Idle 
Cross, and resurfacing works on the N52 
Tullamore 
Bypass 
roundabouts 
will 
commence in June.  
 
Community Involvement Scheme 
The Department of Transport, Tourism and 
Sport proposes to continue the Community 
Involvement Scheme in 2020 and 2021. 
Local Authorities are invited to apply to the 
Department 
for 
CIS 
funding 
before 
September 2019. The Roads section will 
write to elected members and potential 
schemes should be discussed with the Area 
Engineers in the Municipal Districts. 
 
Shannonbridge Service Block Upgrade  
This was opened for use on 15th May. The 
original shower & toilet block, built by OCC 
in 1994 next to the River Shannon, has been 
operating annually during the tourist season 
aimed at accommodating tourists arriving by 
boat. The upgrade works, funding by Offaly 
Local Community Development Committee, 
Birr MD, and Waterways Ireland, included 
re-wiring and re-plumbing; installation of 
new internal fixtures, fittings, and finishes 
including a wheelchair accessible room. The 
facility has an electronic access system in 
line with other Waterways Ireland facilities 
along the River Shannon.   
 
The Town and Village Renewal Schemes  
Work is ongoing in Shinrone, Banagher, 
Cloghan and Rhode. Shannonbridge, Leabeg 
(Boora) and Croghan will commence in 
June. Clara and Ballycumber are currently on 
public consultation for Part 8 planning. 
Ferbane, Kinnitty, Daingean, Edenderry, 
Geashill are at the planning and design stage

Community Enhancement Programme 2019 
The Community Enhancement Programme 
2019 was launched on the 12th April 2019. 
Offaly County Council had been allocated 
€138,550 in CEP funding. CEP programme 
is designed to work around groups across the 
country 
to 
enhance 
facilities 
in 
disadvantaged areas. Any ‘not for profit’ 
community or voluntary group could apply. 
Commercial organisations and individuals 
are not eligible. There were 198 applications 
made to the CEP 2019. There was €1.1 
Million value of applications received. From 
the recommendations of an LCDC Sub-
Committee the fund was dispersed with 69 
grant allocations made to Small Capital 
Projects, 62 grant allocations made to 
Medium Capital Projects. Letters of Offer 
are been sent out with a return deadline of 5th 
July 2019. Funds to be drawn down by

LIBRARY SERVICES 
 
Comic Con  
Tullamore library hosted its inaugural Comic 
Con on Saturday 18th May.  The library was 
transformed to include a number of stalls, 
Viking Re-enactment group from Rhode, 
make-up and drawing workshops, animation 
demonstrations, game stations and much 
more.  In a six hour period (10am – 4pm) 
1,525 people visited the library maybe for the 
first time.  For many, this was their first time 
in Tullamore Library.  Both Offaly Library 
and Offaly County Council Facebook pages 
highlighted and promoted the event.  This 
increased the public awareness and increased 
the profile of the event.  The collective 
presence on Facebook reflects the activities 
in all department of Offaly County Council   
 
Cruinniu na nÓg 
Offaly Library Service is working on the 
Cruinniu na nÓg programme on behalf of 
Offaly County Council.  This is a Creative 
Ireland initiative.  There are 27 events 
organised around the county this weekend.  
There are 6 launches of longer term projects 
which reflect many creative outlets including

Summer Stars 2019 
Summer Stars is an annual programme 
which promotes children’s literacy and 
reading development. It takes place during 
the summer months and focuses on 
encouraging 
children 
to 
develop 
and 
continue the reading habit during their school 
holidays.  This programme will be launched 
on the 15th June alongside Cruinniu events.  
Over 1,000 children took part in 2018.  The 
target set for 2019 is 1,200 children.   
 
Recycling Rocket competition  
There is Offaly county wide “Make your own 
rocket using only recyclable materials” 
competition to make and celebrate the 50 
years since Apollo 11 landed on the Moon.  
There are two age categories:  5-8 & 9-12 
years old. 
The closing date for the competition is 17th 
July 2019 at 5pm.  All entries must be 
delivered to Tullamore Library.  The winner 
will be announced in the 20th July in 
Tullamore Library.  There will be a whole 
host of events in Tullamore library to mark 
this historic day.   
 
LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE 
 
Offaly company Dotser wins Regional 
Enterprise Award 
Tullamore based Dotser has won the award 
for the Mid-East Region at this year’s 
National Enterprise Awards, organised by 
the Local Enterprise Offices to celebrate 
Ireland’s best small businesses. 
Dotser Ltd. was founded in 2000 by 
Loughnan 
Hooper 
providing 
web 
development and marketing services to the 
SME business sector. Dotser now employs a 
team of 9 professionals, delivering a suite of 
online software and related web services to 
over 
300 
clients 
throughout 
Ireland. 
Congratulating the local winners, Orla 
Martin, Head of Enterprise with Local 
Enterprise Office Offaly said: “Dotser are 
very deserving winners of this year’s 
Regional Enterprise Award and the team in 
Local Enterprise Office Offaly are very 
proud of their achievements.” 
 
I-LOFAR Education Centre Launch 
The I-LOFAR Education Centre in Birr was 
officially opened on 30th May 2019 by 
Professor Dame Jocelyn Bell Burnell. The 
newly opened I-LOFAR Education Centre 
will provide STEM educational training & 
outreach projects in the Midlands Region. It 
will help increase Science Capital & 
encourage students pursue careers in science 
and innovation in the Midlands. Offaly 
County Council has been working with 
Professor Peter Gallagher of DIAS; Trinity 
College, 
Dublin; 
and 
the 
I-LOFAR 
Consortium to develop these opportunities. 
Offaly County Council applied for and was 
successful in securing a grant of €316,870 
towards the development of I-LOFAR 
Education 
Centre, 
refurbishing 
Mount 
Palmer barn. The funding issued from the 
Department of Rural and Community 
Development under the Rural & Economic 
Development Zone (REDZ) Scheme.

have any queries or require any information, 
please feel free to contact ONE Network Co-
ordinator Caroline Spollen on 087-8397729.

Lean for Small Businesses Training & 
Mentoring Programme, 10 & 17 June 
The programme will be delivered through 
two full day group workshops which will 
take place in Portarlington Enterprise Centre 
on 10th & 17th June 2019. The lean process 
is a method for creating a more effective 
business by eliminating wasteful practices 
and improving efficiency. This is a joint 
programme between Laois and Offaly Local 
Enterprise Offices with six businesses from 
each county participating. In addition to the 
2 day programme, each participant will 
benefit from 5 half days on site consultancy.
